Automates task-to-production workflows, PR management, code cleanup, performance investigation, drift detection, and multi-agent code review. Includes agnix for linting agent configurations. summary.one_liner: AgentSys is a modular orchestration runtime for AI coding agents that bundles plugins, agents, and skills for task-to-production workflows such as issue handling, PR landing, code cleanup, and agent-config linting.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes 11 plugins, 5 agents, and 14 skills that compose into structured development pipelines with phase gates and state that persists across sessions. The main commands are /foreman (works a GitHub issue queue using worktree subagents, from claim through review to squash merge), /deslop (regex, multi-pass, and optional CLI-tool detection of AI slop such as debug statements, TODOs, and stub functions, with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW certainty levels), /agnix (lints agent configuration files such as SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, hooks, and MCP configs, with SARIF output for GitHub Code Scanning), /learn (researches a topic and writes a learning guide with an index), /banthis (persists banned agent behaviors into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md), and /skillers (reads Claude Code transcripts to suggest automations). Separate skill-only plugins cover glide-mq message-queue development and migrations from BullMQ and Bee-Queue, plus Mojo and Ada/SPARK. Installation is through a Claude Code marketplace or an npm installer that supports Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Cursor, and Kiro.
use_cases: Work a GitHub issue queue from pick to merge with agents
Clean AI-generated debug statements and placeholder code
Lint SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and hook configs for errors
Persist 'stop doing this' corrections into agent instruction files
Research a topic and generate a learning guide for agents
Migrate a Node.js job queue from BullMQ or Bee-Queue to glide-mq
how_to_run: npm install -g agnix  # required CLI for /agnix
notable: /foreman has no daemon or state store; GitHub labels, assignees, and comments hold the queue state so several sessions can share it
Detection is split deliberately: regex and AST/static analysis for deterministic findings, LLM calls only for judgment, with certainty levels HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
Each plugin lives in its own standalone repo under the agent-sh org; agentsys acts as marketplace and installer
Supports multiple agent tools (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Cursor, Kiro) from one install
agnix linter lists 457 rules across many agent platforms and can output SARIF for CI
caveats: Several commands need external tools: gh authenticated for GitHub workflows, glab for GitLab, waitfor on PATH and Node 22+ for /foreman
/foreman's run-long feature requires systemd user units, so it is Linux-only
/agnix requires a separately installed agnix CLI
The README is marketing-heavy and includes a third-party sponsor note; the README's own platform-support statements are the main source for compatibility
